"Cloud Smokeping" typically refers to deploying the Smokeping network monitoring tool on a cloud server (like AWS, DigitalOcean, or Google Cloud).
This setup is highly useful for: 1. External Monitoring: Measuring latency and packet loss to your home or office network from an outside perspective. 2. Cloud-to-Cloud Latency: Monitoring the performance between different cloud providers or regions. 3. Uptime Tracking: Ensuring your public-facing services are reachable and stable.
The easiest way to deploy Smokeping in the cloud is usually via a Docker container (like the LinuxServer.io Smokeping image) or using an automated script/cloud-init setup.

"Local smokeping" is not a common term or concept in the context of Smokeping or networking. However, if you're looking for information on running Smokeping on your local machine to monitor your local network performance, Smokeping is a popular open-source tool for that purpose.
Smokeping is a simple but effective tool that allows you to monitor the performance of your local network, including latency, packet loss, and packet counts. It's commonly used for network troubleshooting and performance optimization.
If you're looking to run Smokeping locally, you would typically install Smokeping on your local machine and configure it to monitor your network interfaces. You can then run Smokeping on a regular interval to see how your network is performing.
